item.title: Generalized Images for Brownian First Passage to Monomial Boundaries
item.description: arXiv:2610.30298v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the first passage of Brownian motion to a monomial moving boundary. For every integer degree at least two, we construct a time-independent signed image measure whose heat potential is the killed Brownian transition density on a nonzero interval of the natural Brownian time scale. The image density is determined by a second-kind Volterra equation in the image coordinate, not by the classical Volterra equations in time for the hitting density. Its kernel is an explicit Wright function, and the first-passage density is recovered afterwards from the boundary flux. Exponential bounds establish convergence, while a beta-moment transform connects the Wright kernel with the finite-order differential hierarchy previously obtained from transported moving zeros. A cubic numerical experiment independently checks the resulting density against simulated Brownian paths.
item.dc:creator: Gerardo Hern\'andez-del-Valle

item.title: A note on functional non-central limit theorem for periodic regime-switching stable-like processes
item.description: arXiv:2610.30342v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish a functional non-central limit theorem for regime-switching stable-like processes with periodic coefficients. Our approach relies on stochastic analysis methods, in particular semimartingale characteristics, combined with the ergodic theory of Markov processes. If the set on which the order function achieves its minimum value $\underline{\alpha}$ has positive Lebesgue measure, then the limit is a rotationally invariant $\underline{\alpha}$-stable L\'evy process. Otherwise, the limit is the zero process.
item.dc:creator: Nikola Sandri\'{c}

item.title: Optimal CLT error bounds in the second order Wasserstein metric via Stein's method for weakly dependent sequences
item.description: arXiv:2610.30352v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We use Stein's method to prove general upper bounds on the second order Wasserstein distance in the CLT for general dependent partial sums $S_N=X_1+\ldots +X_N$. Then we use these estimates to provide optimal $O(N^{-1/2})$ rates for a variety of chaotic dynamical systems and $\phi$- and $\psi$-mixing sequences. Our results for $\psi$-mixing sequences are obtained under the fourth moment condition, which matches the best known results in the iid case. This is the first time that optimal CLT rates of any kind are obtained for unbounded weakly stationary variables under general mixing conditions. We then apply this result and obtain optimal CLT rates $O\left((\text{Var}(S_N))^{-1/2}\right)$ for non-stationary $\psi$-mixing sequences without any growth rates on $\text{Var}(S_N)$. We also obtain close to optimal CLT rates for nonconventional sums and some classes of random dynamical systems with non-uniform decay of correlations
item.dc:creator: Yeor Hafouta, Juho Leppanen

item.title: The longest increasing subsequences of Luce permutations and permutons
item.description: arXiv:2610.30382v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the longest increasing subsequences (LIS) of random permutations distributed under the Luce model with weights $\theta_1^{(n)} \ge \ldots \ge \theta_n^{(n)}$. Our first main result provides a general formula for the growth rate of the LIS. For example, we get that the LIS of Luce permutations with Sukhatme weights $\theta_k^{(n)} = n-k+1$ grows like $\sqrt{n}$. We also give simple conditions for the LIS to be of order $n^\beta$, for any given $\beta\in[1/2,1)$. Our second main result states that, if the weights are of the form $\theta_k^{(n)} = f\big( (k-1)/n \big)$ for a sufficiently regular function $f$, then the LIS divided by $2\sqrt{n}$ converges in probability to a constant $K(f)$ described by a variational problem. Throughout, we make extensive use of coupling techniques; in particular, to prove our second main result, we argue that Luce random permutations behave similarly to random permutations sampled from the ``Luce permuton''.
item.dc:creator: Jacopo Borga, Victor Dubach

item.title: Couplings with prescribed maxima: A short proof of the quasi-copula characterization
item.description: arXiv:2610.30642v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide a short probabilistic proof of the classical characterization of multivariate quasi-copulas, addressing the call for a simpler and more transparent proof expressed by Sempi (2017). Our approach is based on a coupling construction for random variables with fixed marginal distributions and a prescribed distribution of their maximum. In our main result, we show that such a coupling exists if and only if the maximum is stochastically no smaller than each component and the distribution of the maximum is dominated by the sum of the marginal measures. The construction applies to arbitrary distributions and relies only on a decomposition of the maximum law and monotone quantile couplings. A direct consequence of our main result is the existence of copulas with prescribed values along an increasing track.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Ansari

item.title: The Laplace transform of the stationary measure of the open KPZ equation in the shock region
item.description: arXiv:2610.30699v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The stationary increment measure of the open Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation on a bounded interval can be represented as the independent sum of a Brownian motion and another process defined via an explicit Radon-Nikodym derivative with respect to the measure induced by a Brownian motion. In the fan region, its finite-dimensional Laplace transform was previously expressed in terms of the continuous dual Hahn process. The main contribution here consists of computing the finite-dimensional Laplace transform for a range of parameters in the shock region by an analytic continuation argument. As an application, we provide a direct proof of the convergence of the finite-dimensional distributions of the increment height function of open WASEP under the stationary measure in the shock region, by computing the convergence of finite-dimensional Laplace transform without relating to the open KPZ equation.
item.dc:creator: Zoe Himwich, Yizao Wang

item.title: Stationary Half-space Geometric Last Passage Percolation without Random Shift
item.description: arXiv:2610.30739v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive exact formulas for the diagonal distribution of half-space geometric last-passage percolation with a two-parameter family of stationary initial conditions throughout the phase diagram. Unlike previous results, our formulas remove the random shift at the origin. Under critical scaling, we obtain new formulas for the half-space stationary KPZ fixed-point distribution at $x=0$ in the high-density and maximal-current phases. In the low-density phase, we derive a new representation and show that it matches the corresponding formula from the stationary log-gamma polymer.
item.dc:creator: Alessandra Occelli, Jiyue Zeng

item.title: Central limit theorem for the Smoluchowski--Kramers approximation
item.description: arXiv:2610.30835v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the central limit theorem (CLT) for Smoluchowski--Kramers approximation of Langevin equations with state-dependent, possibly non-symmetric friction and multiplicative noise. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first such result, even in the case of constant friction and additive noise. The result differs in an essential way from classical averaging CLTs and reveals a new two-scale fluctuation phenomenon. The normalized difference process retains a persistent fast component and is generally not tight in $C([0,T];\mathbb{R}^d)$, thus the usual continuous-path CLT cannot hold. We derive an exact decomposition of the normalized difference into an accumulated slow fluctuation and a rapidly relaxing velocity correction. The auxiliary slow fluctuation converges to a linear diffusion driven by both the original Brownian motion and an additional independent Brownian noise whose effective covariance is characterized explicitly through a quadratic Poisson corrector. For every fixed $t>0$, the fast correction converges conditionally to its local Gaussian equilibrium. Consequently, the fixed-time fluctuation limit is identified as a Gaussian mixture: $$ \frac{\bar X_t-X_t^\varepsilon}{\sqrt{\varepsilon}} \Longrightarrow \bar Y_t+N^{1/2}(\bar X_t)\xi, $$ where $\bar X_t$ is the overdamped limit, $\bar Y_t$ is the limiting slow fluctuation, $N$ is the covariance of the terminal velocity correction and solves a Lyapunov equation, and $\xi$ is a standard Gaussian random variable independent of $(\bar X_t,\bar Y_t)$. A quantitative convergence rate is also provided. The result fills the remaining gap in the asymptotic theory of the overdamped approximation at the central limit scale, complementing the existing law of large numbers, moderate deviation and large deviation results.
item.dc:creator: Yun Li, Longjie Xie, Li Yang, Qianning Zhang

item.title: Strong uniqueness for fractional stochastic differential equations with sign drift
item.description: arXiv:2610.30889v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Establishing pathwise uniqueness for stochastic differential equations driven by fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H>1/2$ remains challenging, particularly for discontinuous drifts beyond the regularity regimes of existing theories. A canonical example is the sign drift, for which uniqueness fails in the corresponding deterministic equation. In this paper, we complement recent strong existence results by establishing pathwise uniqueness for the equation with sign drift perturbed by fractional Brownian motion for every $H\in(1/2,1)$, thus obtaining strong well-posedness. Our proof develops a new approach based on the infinite iteration of an inequality arising from a fixed-point relation, combined with tail probability estimates exploiting the Gaussian structure of the noise. The methods and results cover a broader class of Gaussian Volterra processes satisfying suitable local nondeterminism and positivity conditions.
item.dc:creator: Ercan S\"onmez, Yuliya Mishura

item.title: Path-dependent rough differential equations in the full step-two range
item.description: arXiv:2610.30931v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the existence of solutions to path-dependent rough differential equations with non-anticipative coefficients whose regularity is formulated in terms of horizontal and vertical Dupire derivatives. Under the same regularity assumptions as in Ananova~\cite{An23}, we develop a new causal Taylor argument and establish a second-order remainder estimate. This removes the regularity loss responsible for the restriction $2\leq p<1+\sqrt{2}$ in~\cite{An23} and extends the existence result to the full range $2\le p<3$.
item.dc:creator: Xing Gao, Nannan Li

item.title: Ultra-hard-edge universality under deterministic preconditioning
item.description: arXiv:2610.31143v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $A_n$ be an $n\times n$ real matrix with iid entries distributed as a fixed centered, variance-one, symmetric subgaussian random variable. For deterministic invertible $M_n$, set $h_n=\|M_n^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}$ and $B_n=M_n^{-1}/h_n$. We prove $\mathbb{P}(s_{\min}(M_nA_n)\le\varepsilon/h_n) =(1+o(1))\varepsilon\Theta_n(B_n)$ as $n\to\infty$, uniformly over $M_n$ and $e^{-cn}\le\varepsilon\le n^{-C}$. Here $\Theta_n(B)=\mathbb{E}\sqrt{nU^\top BB^\top U}$, where $U$ is uniform on $S^{n-1}$. The constants $c>0$ and $C>1$ depend only on the entry law. No condition-number bound or effective-rank assumption is required. The coefficient tends to one for diffuse inverse profiles. For convergent concentrated or spiked profiles, its limit is an explicit Gaussian expectation. The proof combines the submicroscopic comparison of Sah, Sahasrabudhe, and Sawhney with signed-permutation averaging and a weighted comparison for random hyperplane normals. Applications include inverse amplification, square sample covariance matrices with arbitrary deterministic positive-definite population matrices, and independent random environments.
item.dc:creator: Christian E. H\"aggblom

item.title: A local-to-global principle for $f$-divergence homogenization
item.description: arXiv:2610.31164v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the effect of replacing a family of independent statistical experiments by independent repetitions of their average. We give a simple, complete characterization of the $f$-divergences for which this operation increases divergence by at most a constant depending only on the generator, uniformly in the number of observations and the underlying measurable space. The characterization is governed by a local-to-global principle: a comparison restricted to two observations on a binary alphabet already determines the validity of the general inequality. It admits an explicit scalar formulation, which simplifies further for symmetric divergences. The result applies to arbitrary convex generators and requires no differentiability or symmetry assumptions. It recovers the homogenization inequality for total variation and identifies exactly the admissible members of the power-divergence family. In particular, whenever uniform homogenization fails, the obstruction is already present in a family of binary experiments with two observations. Moreover, the global comparison constant is controlled uniformly over generators with a common bound in the local inequality.
item.dc:creator: Aryeh Kontorovich

item.title: Atomic limits of empirical measures of interacting particle systems with self-duality
item.description: arXiv:2610.31319v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the fixed-particle limit of empirical measures for a unified self-dual family of conservative particle systems on $\mathbb{Z}^d$: independent random walkers, the symmetric exclusion process, and the symmetric inclusion process. For a fixed number of particles $k$, under diffusive space-time scaling parametrised by $n$, we prove that as $n\to\infty$ the normalised empirical measure converges in $D([0,T],\mathcal{M}_1(\mathbb{R}^d))$ to an atomic empirical measure carried by $k$ independent diffusions, with constant covariance determined by the microscopic jump kernel. Equivalently, the limit is the unique atomic solution of the Dean-Kawasaki martingale problem with mass quantisation $1/k$. In particular, exclusion and inclusion have the same fixed-$k$ atomic limit as independent walkers: the interaction contributes only through microscopic near-collisions, whose rescaled occupation time vanishes. The proof combines self-duality, consistency-based reduction to two particles, and Green-function estimates for finite perturbations of symmetric random walks.
item.dc:creator: Mario Ayala, Nicolas Dirr, Johannes Zimmer

item.title: Concentration inequalities for vector-valued martingales
item.description: arXiv:2610.31449v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish several deviation inequalities for the norms of vector-valued martingales, achieving bounds of the same quality as those available in the classical one-dimensional setting. Our results extend and refine previous work by Pinelis (1994) and Hayes (2005) in this area.
item.dc:creator: Tomas Ju\v{s}kevi\v{c}ius, Matas \v{S}ileikis

item.title: Bulk stability of bimolecular stochastic chemical reaction networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.31550v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish criteria for stability in the bulk of planar stochastic chemical reaction networks with mass-action kinetics. Using Poincar\'e compactification, we characterize the asymptotic drift and show how stochastic fluctuations can prevent escape along transversally repulsive branches of the limiting deterministic flow. We construct a Lyapunov function by combining local estimates near these branches with dissipative estimates in the neighboring regions. The criteria cover a wide class of networks and in particular apply beyond weakly reversible and strongly endotactic networks. Together with compatible boundary estimates, these criteria imply positive recurrence.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Agazzi, Lucie Laurence

item.title: Upper tail large deviations of regular subgraph counts in sparse random regular graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.31590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a $\Delta$-regular connected graph $H$ we obtain the upper tail large deviations speed and rate function for the number of copies of $H$ in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$, a random $d$-regular graph on $n$ vertices, in the regime $np^{\Delta/2} \gg (\log n)^{1/(v_H-2)}$ and $p \ll 1$, where $p:=d/n$ and $v_H$ is the number of vertices, and also identify the typical structure of $\mathbb{G}_n^d$ conditioned on this upper tail event. For $\Delta \geq 3$, the speed and the rate function are same with those in the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi setting. In contrast, for $\Delta=2$ (i.e.~in case of cycles), due to the degree constraint in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$, although speed remains the same the rate function turns out to be different. Moreover, conditioned on the upper tail event of cycle counts in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$, we show that the random graph contains a disjoint collection of clique and biclique like structures with probability approaching to one, a stark contrast compared to the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi setting. In the complementary regime, i.e.~for $1 \ll n^{v_H}p^{e_H} \ll (\log n)^{\alpha^*_H/(\alpha^*_H-1)}$, where $e_H$ is the number of edges in $H$, $\alpha^*_H$ is the fractional independence number of $H$, and $H$ is a strictly balanced graph (and thus including the regular case), we show that the upper tail large deviations speed and rate function for the number of copies of $H$ match with those in the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi setting. In this regime, we further show that almost all of the unlabeled copies of $H$ conditioned on the upper tail event are edge disjoint.
item.dc:creator: Anirban Basak, Shaibal Karmakar

item.title: Hydrodynamic and Stochastic Limits of Space-Time Hawkes Processes
item.description: arXiv:2610.31604v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the large-scale behavior of critical and nearly critical space-time Hawkes processes initialized by a prescribed Poisson field of past events. The density of this initial field separates three macroscopic regimes. In the high-density regime, fluctuations average out and the event measure converges to a hydrodynamic limit which is a deterministic diffusion profile. At the fluctuation threshold, random branching remains visible and produces a measure-valued stochastic limit. Below the threshold, the rescaled event measure vanishes locally even though its mean generally remains nontrivial, with rare large clusters accounting for the surviving mean. For reproduction delays with finite mean, the critical limits are described by heat flow and the occupation measure of a branching diffusion. A nearly critical perturbation introduces linear decay without changing the three-regime structure. Heavy-tailed delays lead to a different balance between time and space: the mean follows a fractional diffusion law, the stochastic limit is a superprocess occupation measure on time-space, characterized by a nonlinear fractional equation, and the past persists as a temporal memory term. We also determine how the scaling of the Poisson past must be matched to the observation scales and show that, in one spatial dimension, a shorter observation window recovers stochastic behavior hidden in the sparse regime. The results allow bounded initial profiles with possibly infinite total mass and describe the limits directly at the level of locally finite event measures.
item.dc:creator: Fuqing Gao, Yingli Wang, Lingjiong Zhu

item.title: The Critical 2D KPZ Process
item.description: arXiv:2610.31614v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work constructs a non-trivial solution to the ill-defined two-dimensional Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) equation at criticality: a distribution-valued stochastic process on the plane, which we call the Critical 2D KPZ Process. It arises as the limit in law of centred log partition functions of two-dimensional Gaussian directed polymers at criticality, viewed as discretised KPZ solutions. It is also a measurable function of the Critical 2D Stochastic Heat Flow (SHF) via a renormalised Cole-Hopf transformation, obtained as the limit of the centred logarithm of the spatially mollified SHF as the smoothing is removed. The Critical 2D KPZ process is non-Gaussian and its covariance displays a log-log blow-up near the diagonal. Gaussian fluctuations emerge when averaging on shrinking spatial scales. The results presented here were obtained through extensive interactions with generative AI (ChatGPT 5.5, 5.6 and 6); see Appendix C for more details. The proof builds on key recent and older advances in our field, combined in novel ways with substantial AI input. We view this manuscript as a "community project" that represents more than a decade's collective effort. We have worked on making the presentation as accessible as possible, highlighting the main ideas and their relations to the literature.
item.dc:creator: Quentin Berger, Francesco Caravenna, Jeremy Clark, Alexander Dunlap, Yu Gu, Ziyang Liu, Shuta Nakajima, Rongfeng Sun, Li-Cheng Tsai, Zuodi Xie, Nikos Zygouras

item.title: On the direct SLE-martingale approach to the integrability of Conformal Loop Ensembles
item.description: arXiv:2610.31648v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is about the derivation of "integrability results" (i.e., for example, explicit formulas for the probability of events involving a few marked points) for Conformal Loop Ensembles, that are the (conjectured) scaling limits of discrete crititical planar lattice models from Statistical Physics. We discuss the explicit solutions to the PDEs provided by the original SLE/CLE martingale approach that AI now makes it possible to uncover. This provides short and direct new proofs of a number of formulas that have recently been derived based on Liouville quantum gravity, conformal field theory or Coulomb gas methods, and also makes it possible to derive some new ones. We briefly illustrate this with the examples of the backbone exponent and annulus crossing probabilities for critical percolation, but this direct approach seems to apply to a wide class of observables of two-dimensional systems related to conformal field theories.
item.dc:creator: Jason Miller, Wendelin Werner

item.title: Combinatorial formulas for the multivariate Markov-Krein transform
item.description: arXiv:2610.30155v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this work, we study the Markov--Krein correspondence in both the univariate and multivariate settings. Our main result provides an explicit moment--moment formula expressing the multivariate moments of the inverse Markov--Krein transform in terms of the multivariate moments of the Markov-Krein transform via cyclic interval partitions. We also derive moment--cumulant relations involving classical, Boolean and free cumulants.
item.dc:creator: Julian Zazueta-Obeso

item.title: Advance versus Spot Selling in Queueing Systems: the Effect of Uncertainty Sources
item.description: arXiv:2610.30156v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop an unobservable M/M/1 queueing model to analyze advance selling and spot selling under uncertainty. Customers are heterogeneous in waiting costs, drawn from a uniform distribution. We disentangle two fundamental sources of uncertainty: customer valuation and service capacity. We derive the respective revenue functions for both advance and spot selling strategies and compare their performance. Our analysis reveals that advance selling is more profitable when customer valuations are uncertain. Conversely, spot selling emerges as the more profitable strategy when uncertainty originates from service capacity. When both sources are present, our numerical experiments suggest that the preferred regime depends on the relative dispersion of the two uncertainties: advance selling tends to be favored when valuation uncertainty is sufficiently pronounced relative to capacity uncertainty, whereas spot selling tends to be favored when capacity uncertainty is more pronounced. These results highlight how the origin and magnitude of uncertainty shape the optimal selling strategy in service queues and offer practical guidance for platforms and service providers deciding between advance and spot selling.
item.dc:creator: Yumeng Liu, Dongyuan Zhan

item.title: Exact Realization of Edge and Induced Three-Vertex Subgraph Counts
item.description: arXiv:2610.30166v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The study of three-vertex subgraph densities has developed along two complementary lines: exact finite realization in large graphs of a given order, and asymptotic approximate realization by sequences of graphs. We bridge these viewpoints for the edge density and the four induced three-vertex subgraph densities. By analyzing local modifications of finite samples from graphons, we show that, for any nonempty subset of these densities, every asymptotically feasible target vector lying a fixed positive distance from the boundary of the corresponding feasible region is realized exactly by a graph of every sufficiently large order, subject only to the natural arithmetic constraints. Thus, in the interior of these feasible regions, asymptotic feasibility implies exact finite realizability up to the unavoidable arithmetic obstructions.
item.dc:creator: Hillel Schein

item.title: Differentially Private Synthetic Data via Generalized Moment Matching
item.description: arXiv:2610.30196v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-differentially private synthetic data for arbitrary databases of $n$ records in $[-1,1]^d$ under a specified integral probability metric (IPM). We introduce generalized moment matching, which estimates moments privately, fits a probability measure, and samples synthetic records. A general error theorem applies when moment error controls the target IPM. This framework extends Chebyshev moment matching for $1$-Wasserstein distance and smooth queries. We apply the framework to maximum mean discrepancy with Matern and Laplace kernels and a two-layer ReLU neural tangent kernel.We also obtain guarantees for sliced Wasserstein-$1$ and the IPM induced by norm-bounded ReLU networks. With sufficiently many synthetic records,these rates are minimax optimal up to logarithmic factors for fixed dimension.
item.dc:creator: Rundong Ding, Yiyun He, Yizhe Zhu

item.title: Bridge change-of-measure for propagator estimation of diffusions
item.description: arXiv:2610.30213v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The propagator of one-dimensional diffusions has relevant applications in statistical inference and across many disciplines. Yet it is obtained in closed form only for very few simple models. Here we analyze an importance sampling strategy based on a bridge change of measure to estimate propagators: paths are generated under an auxiliary diffusion whose bridge between the two fixed boundary points is easy to generate, and the target propagator is recovered through a Radon-Nikodym derivative or likelihood ratio correction derived from Girsanov's theorem. This method overcomes the main limitations of the crude Monte Carlo estimator, which relies on binning in state space, introducing bias and becoming inefficient with rare transitions. We apply the method to a range of benchmark processes and show that the bridge-based estimator matches the accuracy of crude Monte Carlo with orders of magnitude fewer sample paths. Finally, we elaborate on discretization schemes for the Radon-Nikodym derivative and on approximations to the best-in-class change of measure, both of which increase the efficiency of the method.
item.dc:creator: Javier Aguilar, Riccardo Gatto

item.title: Ergodic Linear-Quadratic Optimal Control with Stochastic Coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2610.30219v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate ergodic linear-quadratic optimal control problems with stochastic coefficients and introduce the associated stochastic ergodic Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation, in which the classical ergodic constant is replaced by a random process $\lambda$. We establish well-posedness of the equation and show that $\lambda$ characterizes the optimal ergodic costs for a general class of averaging kernels, including those corresponding to normalized finite-horizon and discounted costs. For random-periodic coefficients, we construct a random-periodic solution and show that the optimal ergodic costs associated with all admissible averaging kernels coincide. We also establish stability of the optimal ergodic costs under perturbations of the coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Xuyang Lin, Nizar Touzi

item.title: Dynamics of the Liquidity Profile in Concentrated Liquidity Provision: An SPIDE Approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.30539v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We model the dynamics of the liquidity profile in Uniswap~V3 and other concentrated-liquidity automated market makers with a stochastic partial integro-differential equation (SPIDE). The profile, the aggregate of all provider positions across tick space, evolves under a degenerate Sturm--Liouville operator, which encodes mean-reverting concentration around the market price, coupled with a Hilbert--Schmidt integral operator, which captures nonlocal redistribution driven by provider repositioning. We establish existence and uniqueness of the mild solution in a weighted $L^2$ space built on the Gegenbauer eigensystem, and reduce the SPIDE to a coupled system of linear stochastic differential equations whose low-order modes describe the level, slope, and curvature of the profile. Pairing the SPIDE with a log-price process yields tractable expressions for pool reserves, pool value, and loss-versus-rebalancing under Ornstein--Uhlenbeck-type and Black--Scholes-type noise. A finite-rank calibration in a fixed reference frame, applied to three Uniswap pools, gives interpretable estimates and lowers active-band forecast error relative to a martingale benchmark on the two pools compatible with the stationary specification. On the third pool, out-of-sample diagnostics are consistent with nonstationarity, which motivates price-aware and time-varying extensions.
item.dc:creator: Cheuk Yin Lee, Jimmy Risk, Shen-Ning Tung, Tai-Ho Wang

item.title: Optimal Mixing for Local Edge-Coloring Dynamics on Trees
item.description: arXiv:2610.30625v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the mixing time of two local Markov chains for uniformly sampling proper edge colorings of trees. For a tree with $n$ vertices and maximum degree $\Delta$, we establish optimal mixing-time bounds for the single-edge Glauber dynamics when $q\ge\Delta+2$ and for the neighboring-edge heat-bath dynamics when $q\ge\Delta+1$. Both chains mix in $O_\Delta(n(\log n+\log(1/\varepsilon)))$ steps, uniformly over the number of colors $q$. These bounds are tight in their dependence on $n$ for fixed $\Delta$. Our proof establishes log-Sobolev inequalities through local color release, reusable recoloring buffers, and component entropy mixing. The two dynamics require different local constructions: a two-spare-color buffer for single-edge updates and a second-layer controller for neighboring-edge updates. The resulting entropy analysis applies to general bounded-degree trees, including regimes where worst-case spatial mixing fails.
item.dc:creator: Haoran wang

item.title: Multiple Stopping and Exercise Boundaries for American Put Options
item.description: arXiv:2610.30637v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This article studies a finite-horizon American put option with up to $m$ exercise rights under the risk-neutral Black--Scholes model, where consecutive exercises must be separated by a prescribed refractory period $\delta>0$ and unused rights may expire. For each number of remaining rights, we show that optimal exercise is characterized by a single exercise boundary and that these boundaries are ordered by the number of remaining rights. We prove optimality of the first boundary-hitting time and establish local Lipschitz continuity of the exercise boundaries within each open deadline strip. Away from the deadlines, we derive smooth fit, the associated quasi-variational inequality and free-boundary formulation, an early-exercise-premium representation, recursive Volterra-type boundary equations, and a verification theorem. We also extend the recursive formulation to an independent random termination time, thereby allowing for exogenous termination of the option contract.
item.dc:creator: Katsunori Ano

item.title: On Arithmetic-Progression Biases in Random Partitions: Limiting Laws and the Li-Zhao Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.30700v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\cR=\{r+jm:j\geq0\}$ and $\cS=\{s+jm:j\geq0\}$ be disjoint arithmetic progressions of positive integers, and choose a partition of $n$ uniformly at random. We determine the limiting probability that the number of parts in $\cR$ is larger than the number of parts in $\cS$. More precisely, if $a=r/m$ and $b=s/m$, then this probability converges to $I_{1/2}(a,b)$, the regularized incomplete beta function. We prove the stronger distributional statement that, after multiplication by the partition saddle-point parameter, the difference of the two numbers of parts converges to $m^{-1}(\log G_b-\log G_a)$, where $G_a$ and $G_b$ are independent gamma variables. The proof uses the Boltzmann conditioning device for random partitions, a $q$-gamma evaluation of the unconditioned characteristic function, and a uniform Fourier estimate showing that conditioning on the total size does not change the limit. We also evaluate the finite-truncation limit studied by Li and Zhao. The two evaluations coincide, proving their conjecture on the commutation of the truncation and large-size limits.
item.dc:creator: Jiyou Li, Sicheng Zhao

item.title: Sparse power spectrum for passive scalars under Pierrehumbert flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.31241v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the long-time Fourier distribution of driven passive scalars transported by an incompressible alternating shear flow (the Pierrehumbert flow) subjected to IID random phase shifts, in the regime of strong shear-strength. With a novel and self-contained proof, we establish (i) a quantitative version of the cumulative Batchelor's law; (ii) quantitative negative regularity mixing estimates; and (iii) a strong form of `sparsity' -- unevenness in the distribution of Fourier mass in radial sectors in frequency space. Our method uses the strong shear-strength assumption to handle a purely deterministic scalar driving term.
item.dc:creator: Alex Blumenthal, William Cooperman

item.title: Radial $\Phi^4$ models in supercritical regimes
item.description: arXiv:2610.31267v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the $\Phi^4_d$ measure under radial symmetry on the unit ball, formally given by $$d\rho(u) = \frac 1 Z \exp\Big( - \frac 14 \int_{B_1} |u|^4 dx - \frac 12 \int_{B_1} |\nabla u|^2 dx\Big) d u, $$ where $u$ is restricted to radially symmetric functions with 0 boundary conditions. We prove that for every dimension $d$, there exists such a measure, which is concentrated on $L^p(B_1)$ for every $p < \frac{2d}{d-2}$ (for every $p < \infty$ if $d \le 2$). Furthermore, we show that these measures are not Gaussian, and when $d \ge 4$, they are singular with respect to the underlying Gaussian measure. We achieve this result by first defining the measure $\rho^+_\delta[\lambda]$ on the shell $\{\delta \le |x| \le 1\}$, $0 < \delta < 1$, with a boundary condition on the sphere of radius $\delta$ of the form $u|_{\{|x| = \delta\}} = \lambda$. Then we prove that this measure satisfies a variational formula, and use it to show moment bounds which are uniform in the boundary value $\lambda$. A crucial ingredient in this argument is the fact that every solution of the elliptic equation $-\Delta u + u^3 = 0$ on the annulus $\{ \delta \le |x| \le 1 \}$ satisfies uniform bounds inside the domain, independently of the boundary conditions.
item.dc:creator: Tadahiro Oh, Leonardo Tolomeo, Nikolay Tzvetkov, Yuzhao Wang

item.title: Gradient Discrete Schrodinger Bridge Matching for Peptide Generation
item.description: arXiv:2610.31361v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The optimal control of a discrete Schr\"odinger bridge is a discrete gradient, a difference of vertex potentials, but recent models such as MadSBM instead learn a free control on the edges by cross-entropy. We prove that this leaves the action uncontrolled: cross-entropy identifies the control only up to a state-dependent shift (a gauge), and the action is $\operatorname{KL}(r\|p)$ plus a gauge term the loss never constrains. We propose GDSBM, which writes the control as a difference of vertex potentials and adds the action to the loss; pinning the gauge costs no expressiveness and makes the action a property of the model, so the penalty acts on the model and not on the gauge. On peptide generation our MadSBM reimplementation has a free-gauge action of order $10^{8}$ for a gauge-fixed value of $6.5$, against $1.5$ for GDSBM, with no quality loss that three seeds can detect. The gradient form also fits guidance, which becomes the addition of a potential: guided toward a net charge of $+3$ at pH~7, GDSBM is closer than MadSBM, over three seeds, to its exact tempered target in total variation at every guidance strength (at $\beta=1$, $81\%$ of samples in the target window against $74\%$, for a target of $97\%$); we claim no statistical significance.
item.dc:creator: Abdallah BenAbdallah, Mohsen Dlala

item.title: Dimension-free regimes for unadjusted Langevin in ridge-separable models: A subspace robust Wasserstein analysis
item.description: arXiv:2610.31431v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Unadjusted Langevin Algorithm (ULA) is widely used for high-dimensional Bayesian inference. Classical analyses in Wasserstein-2 distance predict an asymptotic bias and a mixing time that grow with dimension, but this metric is stronger than necessary for many statistical tasks. We instead analyze the bias in subspace robust Wasserstein distance, which controls the mean and arbitrary low-dimensional marginals and is therefore well suited to observables typically estimated in practice. For ridge-separable potentials formed with i.i.d. data, we prove high-probability bounds showing a bell-shaped mixing profile as the number of data points $N$ varies relative to the dimension $d$. In the overparameterized regime, the effective dimension is the rank $N$ of the data-dependent perturbation, leading to complexity depending on $N$ rather than $d$. In the large-sample regime, Gaussian-perturbation estimates yield dimension-free complexity once $N$ is sufficiently large. In contrast, near the proportional regime $\asymp d$, we prove that dimension-free guarantees are impossible in general.
item.dc:creator: Yuansi Chen, Francesco Pedrotti, Peter A. Whalley

item.title: Random Survivor Sets with Moving Holes in Bedford-McMullen Carpets
item.description: arXiv:2610.31440v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $2\le m < n$ be integers, and let $K(\mathcal{A})$ be the Bedford--McMullen carpet generated by $\{(x,y)\mapsto((x+i)/m,(y+j)/n):(i,j)\in\mathcal{A}\}$, where $\mathcal{A}$ is a subset of $\{0,1,\ldots,m-1\}\times\{0,1,\ldots,n-1\}$. Write $\mathcal{B}$ for the set of occupied columns, and assume that $\#\mathcal{B}\ge2$ and each column contains at least two symbols of $\mathcal{A}$. At each vertex of the column tree $\mathcal{B}^*$, we independently choose one forbidden symbol from $\mathcal{A}$ according to a prescribed distribution. Let $\mathbb{P}$ denote the resulting product measure on $\mathcal{A}^{\mathcal{B}^*}$. This gives a random survivor set $K_\omega(\mathcal{A})$ with $\omega\in\mathcal{A}^{\mathcal{B}^*}$. We show that, for $\mathbb{P}$-a.e. $\omega$, \begin{equation*} \dim_H K_\omega(\mathcal{A})=\frac{1}{\log m}\log\left(\int \sum_{b\in\mathcal{B}}\ell_b(\omega)^{\frac{\log m}{\log n}} d\mathbb{P}(\omega)\right), \end{equation*} where $\ell_b(\omega)$ is the number of surviving symbols in column $b$ at the root.
item.dc:creator: Derong Kong, Cai-Yun Ma, K\'{a}roly Simon

item.title: Improved Bounds for the Entropic Central Limit Theorem in the Log-Concave Case
item.description: arXiv:2610.31493v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mu$ be a log-concave isotropic probability measure on $R^d$ , and let $\mu^n$ denote the law of the normalized sum of $n$ independent random vectors with law $\mu$. We prove that \[ H(\mu^n|\gamma)\leq \frac{C}{n} \min\left\{1+\log(ed)^2H(\mu|\gamma)\ ,\ d\right\}. \] Compared to the previous best known bound, our estimate replaces the polynomial dependence on the dimension by a polylogarithmic one. The proof relies on a new combination of the De Bruijn identity with Eldan's stochastic localization process.
item.dc:creator: Tom Maitre (LMA)

item.title: Multiple SLEs and Dyson Brownian motion: transition density and Green's function
item.description: arXiv:2311.06789v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider multiple chordal Schramm-Loewner evolution (SLE) with $\kappa\in (0,4]$. Under common-time parameterization, we show that the transition density of the driving function of multiple chordal SLEs can be given by the transition density of Dyson Brownian motion and Green's function. This is a companion paper of [FWY24].
item.dc:creator: Chongzhi Huang, Hao Wu, Lu Yang

item.title: Asymptotics of the free path length in the periodic Lorentz gas in the Boltzmann-Grad limit
item.description: arXiv:2401.08158v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the distribution of the free path length in the periodic Lorentz gas in the Boltzmann-Grad limit. For any unimodular Euclidean lattice and any smooth initial velocity distribution, we establish an asymptotic formula for the distribution function of the free path length with a polynomial rate of convergence. The proof combines the dynamical interpretation of the free path length in terms of expanding translates of horospherical orbits on the space of affine lattices, due to Marklof--Str\"ombergsson, with the effective equidistribution results of Kleinbock--Margulis and Kim. This extends the asymptotic formula of Boca--Zaharescu for the planar case to arbitrary dimension.
item.dc:creator: Songzi Li

item.title: Sampling from Spherical Spin Glasses in Total Variation via Algorithmic Stochastic Localization
item.description: arXiv:2404.15651v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the problem of algorithmically sampling from the Gibbs measure of a mixed $p$-spin spherical spin glass. We give a polynomial-time algorithm that samples from the Gibbs measure up to vanishing total variation error, for any model whose mixture satisfies $$ \xi''(s) < \frac{1}{(1-s)^2}, \qquad \forall s\in [0,1). $$ Our algorithm follows the algorithmic stochastic localization (SL) approach introduced in (Alaoui, Montanari, Sellke, 2022) and in fact achieves a more difficult task. Namely, it (approximately) generates a sample path $({\boldsymbol y}_t)_{t\ge 0}$ from the SL process. For large $T$, ${\boldsymbol y}_T/T$ is an approximate sample from the target Gibbs measure, and hence we solve the original problem as a special case. We provide evidence that the condition $\xi''(s) < (1-s)^{-2}$ is sharp for the task of sampling SL sample paths. Furthermore, we prove that it is optimal within a class of generalized SL processes. Remarkably this threshold is close to the conjectured threshold for sampling from the original Gibbs measure. In particular, for the pure $p$-spin glasses it is within an absolute ($p$-independent) constant of the so-called shattering phase transition. Earlier work on related models was suboptimal by a factor diverging polynomially in $p$. A key step of this approach is to estimate the mean of a sequence of tilted measures. We produce an improved estimator for this task by identifying a suitable correction to the TAP fixed point selected by approximate message passing (AMP). As a consequence, we improve the algorithm's guarantee over previous work, from normalized Wasserstein to total variation error. In particular, the new algorithm and analysis open the way to perform inference about one-dimensional projections of the measure.
item.dc:creator: Brice Huang, Andrea Montanari, Huy Tuan Pham

item.title: The smallest singular value for rectangular random matrices with L\'evy entries
item.description: arXiv:2412.06246v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X=(x_{ij})\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times n}$ be a rectangular random matrix with i.i.d. entries (we assume $N/n\to\mathbf{a}>1$), and denote by $\sigma_{min}(X)$ its smallest singular value. When entries have mean zero and unit second moment, the celebrated work of Bai-Yin and Tikhomirov show that $n^{-\frac{1}{2}}\sigma_{min}(X)$ converges almost surely to $\sqrt{\mathbf{a}}-1.$ However, little is known when the second moment is infinite. In this work we consider symmetric entry distributions satisfying $\mathbb{P}(|x_{ij}|>t)\asymp t^{-\alpha}$ for some $\alpha\in(0,2)$, and prove that $\sigma_{min}(X)$ can be determined up to a log factor with high probability: for any $D>0$, with probability at least $1-n^{-D}$ we have $$C_1n^{\frac{1}{\alpha}}(\log n)^\frac{2(\alpha-2)}{\alpha}\leq \sigma_{min}(X)\leq C_2n^{\frac{1}{\alpha}}(\log n)^\frac{\alpha-2}{2\alpha}$$ for some constants $C_1,C_2>0$. The upper bound was derived in a recent work of Bao, Lee and Xu \cite{bao2024phase2} but the lower bound is new and answers a problem posed in that paper in a weaker form. This appears to be the first determination of $\sigma_{min}(X)$ in the $\alpha$-stable case with a correct leading order of $n$, as previous anti-concentration arguments only yield lower bound $n^\frac{1}{2}$. The same lower bound holds for $\sigma_{min}(X+B)$ for any fixed rectangular matrix $B$ with no assumption on its operator norm. The case of diverging aspect ratio is also computed.
item.dc:creator: Yi Han

item.title: Strategic timing of arrivals to a queueing system with scheduled customers
item.description: arXiv:2502.20105v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper examines a single-server queueing system that serves both scheduled and strategic walk-in customers. The service discipline follows a first-come, first-served policy, with scheduled customers granted non-preemptive priority. Each walk-in customer strategically chooses their arrival time to minimise their expected waiting time, taking into account the reservation schedule and the decisions of other walk-in customers. We derive the Nash equilibrium arrival distribution for walk-in customers. We also study the case where early arrivals are allowed and analyse its impact on equilibrium arrival patterns. By analysing various appointment schedules, we assess their effects on equilibrium arrival behaviour, waiting times, and server idle time. Finally, we compare different scheduling policies and evaluate their impact on overall system performance.
item.dc:creator: Wathsala Karunarathne, Camiel Koopmans, Jiesen Wang

item.title: Polynomial Transformations of Jacobi Matrices, Matrix valued Orthogonal polynomials and Random Walks
item.description: arXiv:2509.01761v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study matrix valued orthogonal polynomials whose block Jacobi matrix is $\Theta(J)$, viewed in blocks of size $m=\deg\Theta$, where $J$ is a tridiagonal Jacobi matrix and $\Theta$ is a scalar polynomial. We identify their matrix measure of orthogonality intrinsically as the push-forward, under $\Theta$, of a matrix measure constructed from the original scalar orthogonal polynomials. We formulate reducibility in the push-forward variable and prove that the $2\times2$ Hermite family associated with $\Theta(x)=x^2+\alpha_1x$ is irreducible for $\alpha_1\neq0$ and reducible for $\alpha_1=0$. This problem is motivated by random walks with transition matrix $\Theta(J)$. For these models, we derive scalar and block Karlin--McGregor representations for the powers of $\Theta(J)$. We apply the construction to the mixed one- and two-ball Ehrenfest chain, obtaining explicit spectral measures, spectral multiplicities, and transition formulas, and we conclude with the corresponding $k$-ball and multi-ball extensions.
item.dc:creator: P. Roman, S. Menchon, Y. Yin

item.title: Space-time bounds for the stirring process with births and deaths
item.description: arXiv:2512.12902v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider a one-dimensional symmetric simple exclusion process on the segment $\{-N,\ldots,N\}$, coupled to boundary dynamics that inject particles from the right reservoir and remove particles from the left reservoir, each acting on a window of size $K$. We derive sharp bounds on the space and space-time $v$-functions of arbitrary degree associated with the centered occupation variables. In particular, we establish bounds of order $N^{-1+2\zeta}$ for spatial $v$-functions of degrees $1$ and $2$, of order $N^{-1}$ for degrees $3,\ldots,K$, and of order $N^{-1-\zeta}$ for degrees at least $K+1$, for some sufficiently small $\zeta>0$. For space-time $v$-functions, we obtain bounds of order $N^{-1}$ for total degrees $2$ and $3$, together with improved bounds for higher degrees, incorporating the dependence on the time separation. These estimates provide the quantitative control needed to study the non-equilibrium fluctuations of the model.
item.dc:creator: Panagiota Birmpa, Patr\'icia Gon\c{c}alves, Dimitrios Tsagkarogiannis

item.title: High-dimensional normal approximations for sums of Langevin Markov chains
item.description: arXiv:2512.19496v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Consider the well-known Langevin diffusion on $\mathbb{R}^d$ $$\mathrm{d} X_t = -\nabla U(X_t)\,\mathrm{d} t + \sqrt{2}\mathrm{d} B_t, $$ and its Euler-Maruyama discretization given by $$X_{k+1}=X_k-\eta \nabla U(X_k)+\sqrt{2\eta }\xi_{k+1},$$ where $\eta$ is the step size. Under mild conditions, the Langevin diffusion admits $\pi(\mathrm{d} x)\propto \exp(-U(x))\mathrm{d} x$ as its unique stationary distribution. In this paper, we mainly study the normal approximation of the normalized partial sum $$ W_n = \eta^{1/2} n^{-1/2} \left( \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} X_i- \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} x\,\pi(\mathrm{d} x) \right).$$ To the best of our knowledge, this work provides the first dimension-explicit convergence rates in high-dimensional settings. Our main tool is a novel upper bound for the 1-Wasserstein distance $W_1(W,\gamma)$ via the exchange pair approach, where $W$ is any random vector of interest and $\gamma$ is a $d$-dimensional standard normal random vector.
item.dc:creator: Tian Shen, Zhonggen Su, Xiaolin Wang

item.title: Strong existence for SDEs with singular drifts driven by fractional Brownian motion
item.description: arXiv:2602.04303v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $B^H$ be a $d$-dimensional fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H\in(0,1/2)$. We prove the existence of a strong solution to $$d X_t=b(t,X_t)d t+d B_t^H, X_0=x_0\in R^d,$$when $b\in L^q([0,T];L^p(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb R^d)),2\le p,q<\infty$ and the subcritical Ladyzhenskaya--Prodi--Serrin condition $\frac1q+\frac{Hd}{p}<1-H$ is satisfied. Thus, within the finite-exponent range $p,q\ge2$, the strong-existence result covers the full subcritical region, including the regime $p<2Hd$, where a uniform strong Novikov condition may fail. The proof is based on a compactness criterion for Wiener functionals. Its main ingredients are an exponentially quantitative derivative estimate for the finite-dimensional densities of fractional Brownian motion, a conditional moment estimate obtained through a martingale representation of fractional Brownian motion, and a frequency-localized truncation of the Cameron--Martin shift. These estimates yield uniform Malliavin--Sobolev bounds for smooth approximations of the equation.
item.dc:creator: Jiazhen Gu, Qian Yu

item.title: Geometry of Unimodular Random Hyperbolic Polyhedra
item.description: arXiv:2608.03575v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a geometric and probabilistic theory of unimodular random infinite trivalent hyperbolic polyhedra in $\mathbb{H}^3$, allowing ordinary, ideal, and hyperideal vertices. Our results relate local dihedral geometry to global conformal type and random-walk behavior. A central role is played by a geometric characteristic $L_f(P)$, determined by the dihedral angles incident to a face $f$. We establish the unimodular Gauss-Bonnet identity $$ \mathbb E[L_f(P)]=2\pi-\frac{\pi}{3}\mathbb E[deg(f)]. $$ Together with circle-pattern uniformization, this yields a sharp parabolic-hyperbolic dichotomy governed by the expected geometric characteristic. We also introduce polyhedral soficity and prove that admissible Benjamini-Schramm limits of finite trivalent hyperbolic polyhedra are parabolic. We further establish a quantitative Ring Lemma for regular circle patterns, providing degree-sensitive geometric control without assuming bounded degrees. Combined with unimodular probability methods, this estimate enables us to identify the Poisson boundary of the face random walk and establish positive linear hyperbolic speed. Our results extend the geometric-characteristic theory beyond ideal polyhedra, connecting three-dimensional geometry, unimodular Gauss-Bonnet theory, and stochastic boundary behavior.
item.dc:creator: Huabin Ge, Yangxiang Lu, Chuwen Wang, Tian Zhou

item.title: A general paracontrolled ansatz for singular SPDEs
item.description: arXiv:2608.09700v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We provide a general ansatz for the paracontrolled approach introduced by Gubinelli, Imkeller, Perkowski for treating singular SPDEs. The ansatz proposed covers a large class of equations. It is described via decorated trees that encode its coefficients and its stochastic data. The main novelty is the recursive definition of the paracontrolled stochastic iterated integrals that involve a well-chosen combinatorial set of words. The paralinearisation is performed via a lift of iterated paraproducts to modelled distributions. The main idea is to integrate localised iterated paraproducts in order to get a global object with a good regularity. We also provide a fixed point argument and the renormalised equation with this ansatz when one uses the preparation map formalism that encompasses the BPHZ renormalisation. The last main result is the convergence of the renormalised stochastic data via the BPHZ renormalisation using an adaptation of the spectral gap approach. One obtains in the end a general solution theory for parabolic singular SPDEs via the paracontrolled approach.
item.dc:creator: Yvain Bruned, Nicolas Moench

item.title: Central limit theorem in R\'enyi divergence for lattice random variables
item.description: arXiv:2608.16144v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\{X_i\}_{i=1}^n$ be independent, identically distributed lattice random variables with zero mean, unit variance, and maximal span $h>0$. Let $S_n=(X_1+\cdots+X_n)/\sqrt n$. Let $Z_n$ denote the quantization of a standard Gaussian random variable on the support lattice of $S_n$. We show that the R\'enyi divergence $D_\alpha(S_n\|Z_n)$ of order $1<\alpha<\infty$ tends to 0 as $n\to\infty$ if and only if $D_\alpha(S_{n_0}\| Z_{n_0})<\infty$ for some integer $n_0$ and a sub-Gaussian condition holds. Furthermore, we derive an Edgeworth-type asymptotic expansion of the divergence to arbitrary order. We also show that the R\'enyi divergence $D_\infty(S_n\|Z_n)$ of infinite order tends to 0 as $n\to\infty$ if and only if a sub-Gaussian condition, a curvature condition, and a uniform separation condition hold. These results constitute lattice counterparts of R\'enyi entropic central limit theorems for continuous random variables obtained by Bobkov, Chistyakov and G\"{o}tze (\emph{Ann. Probab.} \textbf{47} (2019), 270--323) and Bobkov and G\"{o}tze (\emph{Ann. Probab.} \textbf{53} (2025), 453--477). Uniform separation is an additional assumption beyond the sub-Gaussian and curvature conditions used in the continuous setting. The failure of uniform separation may cause an exponentially tilted version of $X_1$ to concentrate on a sublattice of max span $kh$ for some integer $k>1$, which yields the lower bound $D_\infty(S_n\|Z_n)\ge\log k$, and hence a failure of the entropic central limit theorem.
item.dc:creator: Zhen Fu, Jiange Li

item.title: Information Percolation and cutoff for Potts Glauber Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2608.26259v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove cutoff with an $O(1)$ window for the continuous-time heat-bath Glauber dynamics of the ferromagnetic $q$-state Potts model on the discrete torus $\Lambda_n=(\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z)^d$ at sufficiently high temperature. More precisely, for every fixed $d\ge2$ and $q\ge3$, there exists $\beta_0=\beta_0(d,q)>0$ such that, for $0<\beta<\beta_0$, the cutoff occurs in an optimal $O(1)$ window centered at \[ t_\star=t_\star^{(n)}:=\frac{1}{2\mathfrak{r}}\log |\Lambda_n|, \] where $\mathfrak{r}\in(0,1)$ is the exact exponential decay rate of the one-site color bias. Thus, the mixing time is determined up to an additive \(O(1)\). It is characterized by the time at which the macroscopic color-density bias from the monochromatic initial condition enters the scale of equilibrium fluctuations. Moreover, our proof shows that the monochromatic initial condition uniquely maximizes the color bias. This is the first implementation of information percolation to prove cutoff for a non-monotone spin system. On a transitive graph, information percolation naturally gives an upper bound on the mixing time of one half of the grand coupling time which is sharp for the Ising model. However, for many non-monotone systems including the Potts model, this misses additional averaging over the update histories giving an upper bound that is off by a constant multiplicate factor. We develop a new framework that treats the information percolation histories as random polymers and show how to average over them to give the effective bias from the initial condition. This accounts for all the additional mixing, recovering a sharp upper bound and cutoff. We believe this approach will be applicable in a much wider range of settings.
item.dc:creator: Seoyeon Yang, Allan Sly

item.title: Moments Comparison Inequalities for Critical 2d Stochastic Heat Flow, Polymers and GMC
item.description: arXiv:2609.12820v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We employ a Gaussian convex inequality developed in [AC15], [Che26], [Gue22], and [FUMPC26] to establish (one sided) moment comparison inequalities for Gaussian multiplicative chaos, directed polymers in Gaussian environment and, in particular, the Critical 2d Stochastic Heat Flow (SHF), including upper bounds on negative moments, as well as similar lower bounds for $p$-th moments with $p\in (0,1)$. For the Critical 2d SHF, averaged over small balls, we also obtain the matching (up to multiplicative constants) complementary bounds. We establish the complementary bounds using a bootstrap argument inspired by [DS10] and a geometric decomposition introduced in [GT26]. Specifically, we prove that for locally averaged SHF, for every $p\in\mathbb R$, the $p$-th moment is, up to multiplicative constants, bounded in both sides by the $\frac{p(p-1)}{2}$-th power of its second moment.
item.dc:creator: Ziyang Liu, Zuodi Xie

item.title: Relaxation and Steady-State Entropy Production for Langevin SPDEs: A Dirichlet-Form Approach
item.description: arXiv:2609.18201v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a Dirichlet-form framework for relaxation and steady-state entropy production in preconditioned Langevin stochastic partial differential equations. In infinite dimensions, the usual Fokker--Planck calculations based on ambient Lebesgue densities and the corresponding probability-current densities are generally unavailable. For the detailed-balance class, a quasi-regular symmetric Dirichlet form on the Gibbs state space yields an exact de Bruijn entropy-dissipation formula for regular densities and an integrated inequality for arbitrary finite-entropy initial laws. Self-adjointness gives detailed balance and stationary path reversal, while a coordinate-martingale criterion identifies the associated process with the prescribed SPDE. For the one-dimensional $\Phi^4_1$ and convex Allen--Cahn-type Gibbs dynamics, we combine the established strong well-posedness theory with direct verification of the logarithmic derivatives, form closure, quasi-regularity and form--SPDE correspondence, and obtain relative-entropy decay bounds with exponents $2$ and $2(1-\lambda/m)$, respectively, with $m>\lambda$ in the latter case. Away from detailed balance, bounded skew-adjoint linear forcing preserves a Gaussian invariant law without requiring commutation between the forcing and covariance. We identify the antisymmetric action on cylinder observables and its Cameron--Martin current and prove that the squared current energy equals the steady-state entropy-production rate defined by forward--reverse path-space relative entropy per unit time, as well as the monotone limit of the Galerkin rates. Under commutation, we additionally obtain an explicit transient Onsager decomposition after a mass quench. Exclusion processes and Gaussian rotors provide finite-state and Gaussian benchmarks.
item.dc:creator: Shuyuan Fan, Yuanke Chen, Lifei Wang, Jinqiao Duan

item.title: Strong freezing in binary perceptron models
item.description: arXiv:2610.06275v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The binary perceptron model concerns the set of solutions obtained by intersecting random half-spaces. One of the most striking physics predictions for this model, going back to Krauth and M\'ezard [KM89] and sharpened in [HWK13, HK14], is strong freezing: typical solutions are at Hamming distance of order $n$ from every other solution. This phenomenon has attracted a lot of attention over the years, partly because of its intricate connections to statistical physics and computational complexity. We prove strong freezing at every positive constraint density for a general class of perceptron models and for any disorder with independent entries of mean zero and unit variance. More precisely, with probability at least $1-e^{-c\sqrt n}$, all but an $e^{-c\sqrt n}$ fraction of the solutions have no other solution within Hamming distance $\delta n$. In particular, our result includes the asymmetric binary perceptron at every margin, for which strong freezing has been a long-standing open problem [KM89,HWK13,HK14], and the symmetric binary perceptron, for which we recover the strong freezing results of Perkins and Xu [PX24] and of Abbe, Li and Sly [ALS21]. Our proof crucially relies on replacing the number of constraints by a Poisson variable, which makes the numbers of constraints cutting out different subsets of the hypercube independent. Since each constraint can only remove solutions, the FKG inequality then decouples the partition function from the event that two nearby configurations are both solutions.
item.dc:creator: Shuyang Gong, Shuangping Li

item.title: Exponential decay of fractional moments in the $H^{2|2}$ model on $\mathbb Z^2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.10982v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For the $H^{2|2}$ model on $\mathbb Z^2$, we show that, at energy zero, the fractional moments of Green functions, $\mathbb E[ G(x,y)^s]$ decay exponentially in the distance between $x$ and $y$, for every constant edge weight $W>0$ and every $0<s<1/2$. Here $ G$ is the infinite-volume Green function of the associated random Schr\"odinger operator. The main ingredient is a quantitative lower bound on the derivative of the mean effective conductance with respect to the edge weights.
item.dc:creator: Jinglin Wang, Xiaolin Zeng

item.title: A paintbox characterization of labeled partitions
item.description: arXiv:2610.29824v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study pairs of labeled random partitions $(\Pi,\tau)$ with a finite label set $E$, which can be thought of as a random mutation and coalescence mechanism of a countable number of blocks. Labeled exchangeable partition probability functions (LEPPFs) are defined via labeled analogues of Kingman's paintbox partitions. They satisfy normalization, symmetry and consistency in a multivariate sense. Under an equivariance condition, a representation for $(\Pi,\tau)$ in terms of labeled paintbox partitions is derived, leading to a full characterization of LEPPFs by a unique probability measure $G$. This representation is extended to jointly exchangeable and consistent transition pairs using a product measure $F \otimes G$. These results yield a one-to-one correspondence between distributions of jointly exchangeable and consistent transition pairs and pairs of exchangeable distributions and LEPPFs.
item.dc:creator: Maximilian Flamm, Martin M\"ohle

item.title: Fekete Points as Norming Sets for Random Holomorphic Sections
item.description: arXiv:2004.02773v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that Fekete configurations associated with a positive Hermitian line bundle over a compact K\"ahler manifold are asymptotically exact norming sets for random holomorphic sections. For every fixed $a>0$, the ratio of the supremum norm of a degree-$k$ section to its maximum on the degree-$\lceil ak\rceil$ Fekete configuration converges to one in probability. This holds for any background K\"ahler form: Fekete equidistribution provides enough sampling points near the maximum of the limiting pointwise variance. We obtain polynomial upper bounds for the tail of the ratio and almost-sure norm comparisons. In contrast, when the limiting variance is nonconstant, we construct separated arrays of cardinality comparable to the section-space dimension for which the ratio converges to a constant strictly greater than one. General separated arrays still satisfy probabilistic norming inequalities with degree-independent constants, and every such array is asymptotically exact if and only if the volume form is proportional to $c_1(L,h)^n$. We also prove a discrete $L^2$ norm comparison with exponentially small exceptional probability. The norm comparisons and convergence statements hold in both the Gaussian and spherical ensembles.
item.dc:creator: Turgay Bayraktar

item.title: Approximating Kemeny's constant via spectral sparsification
item.description: arXiv:2503.13382v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Kemeny's constant of a network quantifies the expected time for a random walk to reach a target vertex chosen according to the stationary distribution, independently of the starting vertex. The purpose of this work is twofold. First, we introduce the class of slightly regular networks, whose orthogonal degree vector is an eigenvector of the Laplacian, and derive an exact expression for Kemeny's constant for this class, extending previous results beyond regular networks. Second, we address the efficient approximation of Kemeny's constant using spectral sparsification. We establish multiplicative bounds relating Kemeny's constant of a network to that of any of its spectral sparsifiers, and use these bounds to design an approximation algorithm. While standard exact approaches based on a full spectral decomposition or on the computation of a pseudoinverse have $O(n^3)$ complexity, our method has complexity $O(n^2\log^{1+o(1)}n)$ for fixed approximation parameters, and is therefore nearly quadratic in the number of vertices even for dense networks.
