item.title: Conditioned stochastic stability of equilibrium states on uniformly hyperbolic sets
item.description: arXiv:2506.15503v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish the conditioned stochastic stability of equilibrium states for H\"older potentials on uniformly hyperbolic sets. While standard stochastic stability characterises measures on attractors, we analyse the statistics of transient dynamics on non-attracting sets by conditioning small random perturbations of the dynamics to not escape from our regions of interest. We prove that as the noise intensity vanishes, the quasi-ergodic measure of the $e^\phi$-weighted process generated by $\e$-small random perturbations of the deterministic dynamics converges to the unique equilibrium state associated with the potential $\phi - \log \left|\det \left. D T\right|_{E^u}\right|$. The results are obtained via perturbative spectral analysis of transfer operators acting on anisotropic Banach spaces and topological hyperbolic dynamics arguments. Furthermore, we extend this framework globally to Axiom A diffeomorphisms with multiple basic sets using dynamical filtrations. This work provides a rigorous characterisation of natural measures on uniformly hyperbolic repellers, which are fundamental in the context of transient chaos. Our results have been formalised in Lean~4.
item.dc:creator: Bernat Bassols Cornudella, Matheus M. Castro

item.title: High-dimensional learning dynamics of multi-pass Stochastic Gradient Descent in multi-index models
item.description: arXiv:2601.21093v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The learning dynamics of Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) are believed to play an important role in influencing the generalization properties of trained models. While the precise dynamics of how online (one-pass) SGD optimizes the population risk are now understood in a broad range of high-dimensional problems, a comparable understanding of multi-pass SGD for empirical risk minimization is still largely lacking. In this work, we develop an asymptotically exact characterization of the dynamics of multi-pass SGD for a non-convex multi-index model, in the high-dimensional regime where sample size $n$ and data dimension $d$ increase proportionally. We consider any sub-linear batch size $\kappa \asymp n^\alpha$ with $\alpha \in [0,1)$ and a commensurate ``critical'' scaling of the learning rate, and show that the coordinate-wise dynamics of SGD admit a novel continuous-time scaling limit, given by a system of dynamical mean-field equations that are driven by a scalar Poisson jump process representing the asymptotic limit of SGD sampling noise. This scaling limit connects several previously disparate theories around SGD, namely (i) the classical interpretation of SGD as an approximation to gradient flow on the empirical risk, (ii) the characterization of online SGD via an autonomous ODE in its overlap statistics, and (iii) the coincidence between multi-pass SGD dynamics and diffusion approximations in least-squares problems. We illustrate how these perspectives are recovered by specializing our result to small learning rates, large sample sizes, and linear models, respectively. Outside of these specializations, the scaling limit of SGD is distinct both from diffusion approximations and gradient flow, and may enable SGD to converge to local optima of the non-convex empirical risk with different statistical properties.
item.dc:creator: Zhou Fan, Leda Wang

item.title: Level 2.5 large deviations and uncertainty relations for self-interacting jump processes: tilting constructions and the emergence of time-scale separation
item.description: arXiv:2603.19411v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Self-interacting jump processes (SIJPs) describe systems with non-Markovian stochastic dynamics in which transition rates depend on empirical observables of the process, which gives rise to long-range memory and feedback. We derive the ``level-2.5'' large deviation (LD) principle governing the joint fluctuations of empirical occupation measure and the flux matrix for a broad class of SIJPs with general functional dependence on an empirical observable. The derivation is based on an exponential tilting construction and reveals a separation between a faster timescale of the microscopic dynamics and a slower timescale of the memory-driven evolution of transition rates, which is expressed through an exponentially discounted LD rate functional. Using this variational framework, we derive kinetic and thermodynamic uncertainty relations that extend classical Markovian bounds to non-Markovian systems, and illustrate their performance with simple examples.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Coghi, Juan P. Garrahan

item.title: Lattice Brownian bees with cooperative reproduction: steady states, collapse, and spreading
item.description: arXiv:2605.29958v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We extend the ``Brownian bees'' model of Berestycki et al.\ (2021, 2022) to cooperative reproduction, $kA\to(k{+}1)A$, of a population of $N$ symmetric random walkers with removal, at each birth event, of the particle farthest from the origin. Working in the limit $N\to\infty$, we formulate a hydrodynamic free-boundary problem for this model. Using this formalism, we determine steady state population densities for all~$k$ and prove their linear stability for $k\le 2$ and instability for $k\ge 4$. In the marginal case $k=3$, there is a whole continuous family of steady states at a single critical ratio of the reproduction and diffusion rates. Above criticality the population undergoes an asymptotically self-similar finite-time collapse to the origin. Below the criticality the population spreads diffusively, but the reproduction remains quantitatively relevant. For $k\ge 4$, the unstable steady state separates regimes of a finite-time collapse and diffusive spreading. Here the collapse dynamics is asymptotically self-similar, and the population density exhibits a scale separation requiring a matched-asymptotic description. Our analytical predictions are confirmed by numerical solutions of the hydrodynamic free-boundary problem and by Monte Carlo simulations of the original microscopic model.
item.dc:creator: Ohad Vilk, Baruch Meerson

item.title: Quartic Fourier-Laplace limits for $(p,q)$-Rogers-Szeg\H{o} polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2607.09150v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove asymptotic formulae for $(p,q)$-Rogers--Szeg\H{o} polynomials with positive real parameters when the leading quadratic term in the logarithmic expansion about the middle coefficient vanishes. For coefficient indices whose distance from $n/2$ is of order $n^{3/4}$, the coefficient ratios have a quadratic--quartic exponential limit. A uniform bound valid for all indices allows the ratios to be summed and gives locally uniform convergence of the centred and normalised generating polynomials to a Fourier--Laplace integral. We also obtain an asymptotic formula for the sum of the coefficients, convergence of all rescaled moments, weak convergence of the normalised coefficient measures, and convergence with multiplicity of the zeros near $w=1$ for which $n^{3/4}\log w$ remains bounded.
item.dc:creator: Per {\AA}hag, Rafa{\l} Czy\.z, Per-H{\aa}kan Lundow

item.title: New link between the fractional p-Laplacian operators and a class of McKean-Vlasov flight type processes
item.description: arXiv:2609.19492v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the existence of a McKean--Vlasov stochastic process with jumps associated to the nonlinear parabolic equation $\partial_t u = \Delta_p u + \Delta_p^s u$ in $\mathbb{R}^N\times(0,\infty)$, where $\Delta_p$ is the $p$-Laplacian and $\Delta_p^s$ is the fractional $p$-Laplacian. Our approach is the following: first, after proving the existence of a solution for the PDE presented earlier, we rewrite it as a nonlinear Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov equation whose measure-valued solution is guaranteed when $p\ge4$. Then we solve the martingale problem associated to our FPKE via a new superposition principle for non-local Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov equations, which only requires an integrability condition on the local coefficients. Finally, thanks to the martingale solution obtained, we derive the existence of a weak solution for the McKean-Vlasov's type SDE with jumps whose infinitesimal generator is a << hybrid version >> of the operator $\Delta_p+\Delta_p^s$.
item.dc:creator: Houssine El Jeddaoui, Dany Nabab

item.title: Deep Truncated FBSDE Method for High-Dimensional Nonlinear PDEs and Fully Coupled FBSDEs
item.description: arXiv:2609.39616v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a deep truncated forward-backward stochastic differential equation (FBSDE) method for high-dimensional partial differential equations (PDEs) and fully coupled FBSDEs. The proposed method combines gradient-truncated iterative decoupling with fictitious-play averaging to separate the forward and backward processes in a coupled framework. This preserves the coupled dynamics while reducing the unstable feedback induced by parameter-dependent forward paths during optimization. Furthermore, we incorporate a pathwise consistency term to create explicit local gradient shortcuts, thereby providing a structural mechanism that may mitigate gradient vanishing. We also derive a residual-based error estimate and establish conditional convergence of the fully discrete numerical approximations under suitable conditions, in which the pathwise consistency loss is not required. Our approach is particularly effective for convection-dominated equations, where the coupled formulation provides a stable representation of nonlinear transport without introducing singular terms into the BSDE. Numerical experiments demonstrate improved accuracy and stability in both low- and high-dimensional problems and robust performance for strongly coupled problems.
item.dc:creator: Xinyu Cheng, Yunzhang Li, Weiran Xiong

item.title: Two-Species Boltzmann--Kac Kinetics with Matsumoto--Yor Nonlinear Collisions: Conserved Energy and Conic Equilibria
item.description: arXiv:2610.18892v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We extend Mark Kac's kinetic framework from single-species Euclidean spaces to a two-species, non-linear interaction space on the open cone $(0, \infty)^2$ governed by the Matsumoto--Yor rational collision involution. We identify a non-linear conserved energy $E(x,y) = x + y + 1/x$ and an invariant conic metric measure $d\mu = \frac{dx \, dy}{x(x+y)}$. By establishing a two-species $H$-theorem, we prove that entropy production vanishes if and only if post-collision velocities are statistically independent ($I(U;V)=0$). In contrast to the transform-domain proof of Letac and Weso{\l}owski~\cite{letac2000}, which relies on joint Laplace transforms of general measures, our approach yields a direct physical derivation in state space via the transformation law for logarithmic gradients and separation of variables. This uncouples the functional-differential system to uniquely characterize the Generalized Inverse Gaussian (GIG) and Gamma distributions as the non-equilibrium thermodynamic equilibria.
item.dc:creator: Yoshiaki Itoh

item.title: A McLennan formula for equiaccessible steady states
item.description: arXiv:2610.26755v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Near equilibrium, the Boltzmann distribution is corrected by the transient irreversible entropy flux, a result known as the McLennan formula. By expanding around equiaccessible steady states instead, we derive an analogue that can hold arbitrarily far from equilibrium. At zeroth order, steady-state occupation is determined solely by local escape rates, yielding a strong form of the active-matter principle of "low rattling." The first-order correction measures the impact of traffic imbalances on the accessibility of each state, marking the onset of nonlocal determinants of relative occupation.
